title: where the deeplink work can make money — and the reporting trap that kills it
excerpt: Desk research on which programs pay for nonce-laundering XSS: Basecamp/HEY on HackerOne ($100-$10,000, with a 2026 cross-account nonce-bypass chain already disclosed) is the closest fit; Intigriti only has Lightspark and Adobe paying publicly. The trap: "CSP headers" is out of scope, but "XSS despite CSP" is not.

title: Server-side trace of the deeplink gadget: positive and negative findings
excerpt: The deeplink gadget in Mercado Libre's home component D interpolates server-rendered deeplink and redirectUrl values into single-quoted JavaScript inside a nonce'd script. Verified against the saved bundle: a mobile User-Agent flips openInApp.shouldRedirect and mounts it anonymously — but a quote nulls redirectUrl, non-UUID d2id nulls deeplink, and </script> is edge-blocked. Sink confirmed, sanitiser confirmed, no execution.

title: Dead end with test accounts and researching a workaround
excerpt: The ATO 2FA challenge test account (userId 1252539217, CHALLENGE_ATO_USER_2, site MCO) returns 302 /login/identification/not-found, suggesting it is expired or removed. Later work showed the deeplink gadget mounts anonymously for mobile UA (and is sanitised), so the account blocker now applies to the seller / second-order path. Workaround paths: seller accounts, personal account (one only, no mass creation), or waiting for program test-user rollout.
